title: Lesson 91 - Let Me Put That in Plain English

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: The formal note says, “Once an immutable export has been generated, a checksum is calculated and the source object is retained outside the import environment.”

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Let me put that in plain English. First, a fixed copy of the selected records is made, and the original catalog is left unchanged.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Good. The checksum does not prove that every description is correct. It helps us detect whether the exported file changes unexpectedly after it is created.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: In other words, it checks whether we are still working with the same package of data, not whether every fact inside the package is true.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Exactly. Next, each old field is matched to a place in the test system: creator to creator, date to date and item number to item number.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Think of it as matching columns on two forms. The analogy helps with structure, although real fields can contain rules that a paper form does not show.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: After the mapping has been applied, the three hundred records are imported into a separate test area.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: What happens first is copying and checking the package; what happens next is matching the fields and loading the test copy.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Then automated checks look for missing item numbers, impossible date formats and record-count differences.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: You don’t need to run those checks yourself; the project team runs them. Volunteers only report a visible error with the item number.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Records that fail a structural check are flagged and set aside. They are not silently corrected or deleted.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: So “flagged” means the team stops that item for review, not that the source record has been judged wrong.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Correct. Some accurate historical descriptions use unusual dates or names, so a warning may identify an exception rather than an error.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: The important limit is that automated checks can find patterns and missing fields, but a person must decide whether the content makes sense.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: A sample is also reviewed manually against the unchanged source. If a mapping rule caused repeated errors, the test batch would be rejected and rebuilt.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Does “rejected” mean the archive is lost?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: No. Only that test import is discarded. Because the source was not overwritten, the team can correct the rule and create another test.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: Then my analogy needs a warning: it is like checking a copied packing list against the original, but the system also applies field rules that a packing list does not.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: That works. An analogy should illuminate one relationship and then state where the comparison stops.

lines.speaker: Robin
lines.text: My final version will give five steps, the volunteer action and three limits. That is plain English without pretending the process is effortless or foolproof.
